title: Learning to read Russian
topicSummary: Content-complete development unit for printed letters: identities, print pairs, look-alikes, signs, and letter-level decoding. Qualified review and the owned-edition mapping are still pending.
mappingNote: Proposed Lesson 1 mapping from the publisher's public table of contents. Owned-edition comparison is not signed, so this unit is not labeled aligned.

objectives.title: Separate Cyrillic letters from Latin look-alikes
Recognize Е Ё Ю Я as a group
Treat Ь Ъ Й as non-ordinary-vowel letters
Match uppercase and lowercase print pairs
Confirm letter sounds in the book
Treat stress as book-marked, not guessed
Complete Lesson 1 work in the owned book

steps.title: Unit 1 — Printed letters
steps.body: This is a proposed Lesson 1 mapping, not an approved owned-edition alignment. The development unit teaches printed letter identities with public-domain letter forms. Example words and model audio are not part of this unit. Qualified review is still pending.
steps.bookDirection: Open your copy to Lesson 1. Use the book for the author's explanations, exercises, and any example words.

steps.title: Identify letters first
steps.body: Work letter shapes, print pairs, and Latin look-alikes before later reading. Transliteration, if you use it, is a temporary support.

steps.title: Cyrillic is a different alphabet
steps.body: Russian is written with 33 Cyrillic letters. Some printed shapes look like Latin letters and are not the same letters. Learn identity first.

steps.title: First vowel set
steps.body: Work these printed pairs: А а, О о, У у, Э э, Ы ы, И и. English sound notes are pending qualified review.

steps.title: Identify А
steps.body: Choose the Cyrillic identity for the printed letter.

steps.title: Low-confusion consonants
steps.body: Next printed pairs: М м, Т т, К к, П п, Б б, Д д, Г г. Confirm each spoken sound in your book. This unit does not play model audio.

steps.title: Identify М
steps.body: Choose the Cyrillic identity for the printed letter.

steps.title: Shape traps
steps.body: These printed letters often fool Latin-alphabet readers: В, Н, Р, С, У, Х. Name the Cyrillic identity. Read this as a review-pending explanation. Worked examples come before the guided choice, and the independent check is separate. A wrong answer returns to this contrast. Activity is not demonstrated ability.

steps.title: Guided contrast
steps.body: These printed letters often fool Latin-alphabet readers: В, Н, Р, С, У, Х. Name the Cyrillic identity. Choose once with the explanation still in view. This is practice, not the independent check.

steps.title: Р is not P
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Н is not H
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: С is not C
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: В, У, and Х
steps.body: Identity check for the remaining look-alikes.

steps.title: Е Ё Ю Я
steps.body: Recognize these printed forms as a group. Exact phonetics belong in your book. Read this as a review-pending explanation. Worked examples come before the guided choice, and the independent check is separate. A wrong answer returns to this contrast. Activity is not demonstrated ability.

steps.title: Identify Е, Ё, Ю, and Я

steps.body: Russian word stress is not predictable from spelling alone. Marked example words are not installed.

title: Everyday phrases, naming things, basic grammar, and gender
topicSummary: Proposed Unit 3 is a development unit awaiting qualified review. It contains admitted records for gender, everyday phrases, and naming, plus separate book self-attestation. It is not installed and the owned-edition mapping is not signed.
mappingNote: Proposed Lesson 3 mapping remains pending. The structural edition facts are unchanged. This proposed curriculum is not an approved alignment.

steps.title: Everyday phrases, naming, and grouping
steps.body: Proposed Unit 3 uses frozen dictionary rows and grammar excerpts for the groups, a small phrase set, and naming items. The owned book remains separate work. Qualified review is pending.
steps.bookDirection: Open Lesson 3 in the copy you own. The app records do not replace that lesson.

steps.title: Read the admitted grouping sentence
steps.body: The frozen page says: So, in Russian, nouns have an intrinsic property called 'gender', which comes in three types: masculine, feminine, and neuter. An ending is not a substitute for the admitted record.

steps.title: Recorded masculine nouns
steps.body: These admitted records are listed as masculine. стол — table. дом — house. го́род — town. брат — brother. The admitted record for друг — friend is also masculine. Learn this recorded label; an ending is not a substitute for the record.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the admitted record. The feedback states the frozen field.

steps.title: Recorded feminine nouns
steps.body: These admitted records are listed as feminine. кни́га — book. вода́ — water. шко́ла — school. рабо́та — work. The admitted record for дверь — door is feminine. Learn this recorded label; do not guess the gender of another word from its ending.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the admitted record. The feedback states the frozen field.

steps.title: Four records in the third group
steps.body: These admitted records are listed as neuter. окно́ — window. письмо́ — letter. молоко́ — milk. мо́ре — sea.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the admitted record. The feedback states the frozen field.

steps.title: Two records the page still places in the first group
steps.body: дя́дя and мужчи́на decline like nouns ending in -а, and they are masculine. Say decline for these nouns. Do not say they conjugate.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the admitted record. The feedback states the frozen field.

steps.title: Review the admitted noun genders
steps.body:
The frozen page says: So, in Russian, nouns have an intrinsic property called 'gender', which comes in three types: masculine, feminine, and neuter. An ending is not a substitute for the admitted record.

These admitted records are listed as masculine. стол — table. дом — house. го́род — town. брат — brother. The admitted record for друг — friend is also masculine. Learn this recorded label; an ending is not a substitute for the record.

These admitted records are listed as feminine. кни́га — book. вода́ — water. шко́ла — school. рабо́та — work. The admitted record for дверь — door is feminine. Learn this recorded label; do not guess the gender of another word from its ending.

These admitted records are listed as neuter. окно́ — window. письмо́ — letter. молоко́ — milk. мо́ре — sea. 

дя́дя and мужчи́на decline like nouns ending in -а, and they are masculine. Say decline for these nouns. Do not say they conjugate.

steps.title: Independent checks
steps.body: These checks use only admitted records. A miss returns to the explanation.

steps.title: Three short greetings
steps.body: These greetings are copied from admitted rows. здра́вствуйте — hello. спаси́бо — thank you. пожа́луйста — please.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the admitted record. The feedback states the frozen field.

steps.title: Three short answers
steps.body: These short answers are copied from admitted rows. да — yes. нет — no. э́то — this is.

steps.title: Two written questions from the frozen page
steps.body: These written questions are exact frozen excerpts. Как дела? — How do you do?/How're things?. Где вы? — Where are you?.

steps.title: Remediation
steps.body: Return to the explanation. Compare the shown form with the admitted record. Do not invent a form that is absent from the record.

steps.title: Independent checks

steps.title: Two naming items from the frozen page
steps.body: These two items are exact frozen excerpts. Do not substitute another word into them. мой стол — my table. моя собака — my dog.

steps.title: Remediation
steps.body: Return to the explanation. Compare the shown form with the admitted record. Do not invent a form that is absent from the record.
